symptom: On MPR v2, a unit written twice in one `WriteTransaction` could commit the wrong bytes: writing A → B → A (A stored) committed B, with ContentsHash describing B, and no error. A → B → B counted the repeat as a landed write. Latent — no current caller writes a unit twice in one transaction (`codec.Store.FlushUnits` writes each map key once, `SaveUnit` is one transaction per unit) — but `WriteTransaction` is public library API
cause: `WriteUnit` reconciles every write against the stored unit (canon.Reconcile, ADR-0008), and on v2 the stored unit is the committed .mxunit; the transaction's own first write sits in `<unit>.mxunit.tmp` until Commit. So the second write of A matched the committed A, was elided as unchanged, and Commit renamed the pending B into place
insight: Found as the control of a different fix: the v1 WriteTransaction deadlock could also have been ended by widening the pool, and the A → B → A test was written to show why that was wrong (a second connection reads the committed bytes). Running the same three writes on v2 showed v2 had the exact failure the rejected v1 fix would have introduced, for a different reason. The invariant is one sentence: **a write in a transaction is reconciled against the transaction's view of the unit, not the committed one** — on v1 a read through the `*sql.Tx` gives that for free, on v2 it has to look at the pending temp file first. Elision is what makes the bug silent: without canon.Reconcile the second write would simply have landed. A → B → B is the companion test, since an over-eager fix (never elide while a write is pending) passes A → B → A
